relationships.subject: NaV1.7 gain-of-function mutations
relationships.evidence_quote: None of these groups had a significantly altered risk of chronic or neuropathic pain.

relationships.subject: NaV1.7 I228M
relationships.evidence_quote: The I228M mutation was not significantly associated with chronic pain (OR = 0.97[0.87–1.08], P = 0.98, N = 1330)

key_findings: Over one-third of reported pathogenic NaV1.7 gain-of-function mutations are carried by ~30% of UK Biobank participants with no increased chronic or neuropathic pain risk or analgesic prescribing.
Variants present in UK Biobank had lower predicted pathogenicity than absent ones, challenging assumed high penetrance of NaV gain-of-function variants.
